A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeCo research despite the changed title and formatting. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E are available and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original WarpBench and OccluBench validation, evaluation of eight video generators, and guided-generation experiments, with additional qualitative results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical studies and adds TartanAir and DL3DV evaluations, controlled-noise experiments, and motion-dependent analyses.

M1.justification: The documented motion and structure cues, scale-invariant fusion, temporal aggregation, and guidance procedure remain unchanged. Equations 1–9 and the backbone choices and guidance schedule in Appendix C are retained. Revised benchmark scores do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V2 adds artifact-free synthetic sequences from TartanAir v2, real videos from DL3DV, and controlled flow/depth corruption scenarios. This substantially extends validation beyond the existing artifact benchmarks and generated videos. WarpBench, OccluBench, and all 80 GeCo-Eval prompts remain.

E2.justification: MEt3R remains the quantitative metric comparator; WorldScore and SegAnyMo remain qualitative comparators. The same eight generators appear in GeCo-Eval. Ground-truth geometry in the new robustness study is an experimental control, not an added competing method.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix B.4 introduce predicted-versus-ground-truth evaluation on approximately 10,000 frame pairs, a 30-scene real-video evaluation, and independently controlled noise sweeps on 200 pairs. They specify alignment, validity filtering, and component-error metrics. Guidance evaluation also adds Total Motion and Mean Motion; the stated existing GeCo-Eval protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds component-error evaluation, synthetic and real noise-floor measurements, and controlled sensitivity tests absent from v1. Figure 6 adds motion-conditioned consistency curves and motion distributions. Table 6 additionally examines whether guidance reduces dynamism, extending the earlier consistency-only quantitative assessment.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 newly specifies sampling seed 42 for the robustness evaluation. The four-seed GeCo-Eval design and mean-plus-standard-deviation motion reporting are retained. Extending that reporting to new results does not establish additional repeated trials or a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Many GeCo-Eval scores change between v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 5. For example, object-centric fused scores change from 0.110 to 0.069 for Sora 2 and from 0.077 to 0.090 for Veo 3.1, reversing their ordering under the same stated protocol. The PDFs do not explain these revisions. Tables 2–3 and the original guidance consistency scores remain unchanged, while robustness, motion-dependent, and guidance-motion results are added.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds mathematical definitions of additive Gaussian flow corruption and multiplicative log-space depth corruption in Equations 20–21. This is a limited formal addition supporting the new experiments. The geometric definitions, fusion, guidance, TPS construction, and motion normalization remain unchanged; no new proofs or theoretical guarantees appear.

C1.justification: The core claims about a differentiable, dense geometric-consistency metric and training-free guidance remain. V2's abstract and introduction additionally claim robustness to estimator errors. WarpBench and OccluBench remain validation datasets but lose their separate contribution bullet, modestly shifting emphasis toward metric validation and evaluation.

C2.justification: V2 replaces v1's interpretation of consistent Veo superiority with similar Sora/Veo consistency and greater Veo dynamism, and adds interpretations of high-motion behavior and estimator noise. Section 6 newly discusses false positives from legitimate object motion, dependence on geometry estimators, and guidance overhead of 2 versus 19 minutes. These substantially expand applicability and limitation analysis.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 supplies reproducibility details for the new validation: camera selection, sampling, median scale alignment, depth bounds, visibility threshold, and noise grids. Appendix D.1/Table A newly lists native frame rates for all evaluated generators, and Section 6 discloses guidance runtime. The existing detailed guidance configuration is retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against video benchmarks and physical-plausibility evaluation, adding literature such as VideoPhy-2 and recent world-model and 3D-generation work. It removes the dedicated motion-segmentation discussion and several associated references while retaining SegAnyMo in Appendix A. This changes the literature framing beyond citation renumbering.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, extensively rewrites the introduction, reorganizes related work into three subsections, and reframes Section 4 around validation. It replaces the standalone conclusion with a discussion containing limitations and moves references after the appendices. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a predominantly single-column layout. Figure 1 replaces the chess example with deformation and occlusion examples; the two dataset illustrations are merged into Figure 3. V2 adds robustness and motion plots, a robustness table, guidance-motion columns, and a native-frame-rate table. Appendix Figures A–E retain their examples.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful estimator validation, motion diagnostics, reproducibility details, and explicit limitations. However, numerous central benchmark scores change without explanation under the retained protocol. The new robustness evidence also contains an unresolved inconsistency: Table 4 reports TartanAir Easy predicted fused error 0.0066 below structure error 0.0075, which Equation 5 would not permit under common averaging. The PDFs do not explain different aggregation that could reconcile this. These uncertainties affect central empirical support, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
